name: shefa
description: Economy domain — value accounting, stewardship, resource flows, and economic coupling. Shefa primarily wraps protocol REA primitives (EconomicEvent, Agreement, Commitment) with economic semantics rather than declaring many new content types.

stewardship-context.description: Narrative context for a stewardship relationship — why this steward cares about this content, what curation work they have done, and how their standing was earned. Category A2 (derived via link from stewardship allocation).

protocolPrimitives._comment: Shefa does not own these types — they are protocol-level REA primitives. Shefa declares the domain-specific coupling: what signals they produce in the economy context, and what observations the protocol should make.

economic-event.description: An REA economic event — a concrete action that changes resource state. Protocol-level (CreateEconomicEventInput). Shefa declares the coupling semantics: every economic event carries value + governance + feedback dimensions.

agreement.description: An REA agreement between parties — commitments exchanged. Protocol-level. Shefa declares metadata shape and coupling: agreements produce obligation tracking and fulfillment signals.

commitment.description: An REA commitment — a promise to perform a future economic event. Protocol-level. Shefa declares how commitments produce obligation signals and how unfulfilled commitments accumulate as negative observations.

resource.description: An REA resource — anything with economic value that can be produced, consumed, transferred, or stewarded. Protocol-level. Shefa declares resource nature dimensions (rivalry, excludability, depletability, fungibility, circularity).

crossPillarCoupling._comment: The conversation between lamad (wisdom) and avodah (action) is where shefa value is created. These couplings declare how value flows across pillar boundaries.

lamad-to-shefa.description: Mastery attestations from lamad produce stewardship eligibility in shefa. You can steward content if you have the requisite wisdom. The attestation gate replaces institutional credentialing.

shefa-to-lamad.description: Value flows back to content stewards who helped develop wisdom. Stewardship standing in shefa produces recognition flows that sustain the teaching economy.

shefa-to-qahal.description: Economic standing informs governance weight. Stewards with demonstrated curation history have governance voice proportional to their contribution, not their attention or wealth.

imagodei-to-shefa.description: Identity attestations establish economic agency. A verified identity (imagodei) is prerequisite for economic participation (shefa). The identity is the economic agent.

STEWARDS.description: The source stewards the target — curates, maintains, reviews, and governs the target content. Stewardship is earned through mastery and sustained curation, not granted by credential.

STEWARDED_BY.description: Reverse of STEWARDS — the source content is stewarded by the target stewardship-context.

FUNDS.description: Economic flow relationship — the source economic activity funds or sustains the target. Value flows from consumption to stewardship.

OBLIGATES.description: The source creates an obligation on the target. Agreements and commitments obligate parties to future economic events.

economic-event-recorded.description: Emitted when an economic event is notarized on the DHT. The foundational signal for value accounting — every value-creating act in the protocol produces this signal.

stewardship-allocated.description: Emitted when stewardship standing is allocated to a content steward. Standing accrues from curation acts (edits, reviews, dispute resolution), NOT from attention or consumption. This distinction is the anti-capture mechanism.

resource-transferred.description: Emitted when a resource changes custodian. Transfer events track the flow of value through the network and drive circulation health observations.

obligation-fulfilled.description: Emitted when a commitment or agreement obligation is fulfilled. Builds trust standing and drives obligation-fulfillment observations.

custodian-attestation.description: Emitted when a custodian's stewardship is attested by the community. Peer attestation strengthens stewardship standing and gates governance participation.

insurance-claim.description: Emitted when a resource insurance claim is filed. Insurance mutuals track claims as resource consumption events that trigger community response.

distribution-health.description: Are value flows equitable? Measures whether economic activity is broadly distributed or concentrating in few hands. Negative polarity: the protocol watches for capture.

cost-accumulation.description: Are externalities building up? Tracks whether economic activity is creating unaccounted costs — environmental, social, or systemic. The circularity deficit accumulator drives infrastructure to close loops.

obligation-fulfillment.description: Are commitments being honored? Positive observation that tracks the rate of obligation completion across agreements.

stewardship-effectiveness.description: Does curation help or hurt? Negative polarity: the protocol watches for stewards whose curation degrades rather than improves content. Measured by downstream learner outcomes after steward edits.

stewardship-concentrated.description: Single steward controls disproportionate share of domain content. Anti-capture warning signal.

curation-improves-content.description: Steward curation correlates with improved learner outcomes on the content they curate.

curation-degrades-content.description: Steward curation correlates with worsened learner outcomes — content quality declining under their stewardship.

columnMapping._comment: Keys are snake_case DB column names. Values are dotted payload paths or $-prefixed projector-derived sources.

rules.name: household_topology
rules.description: Members + their devices for a given household
rules.datalog: household_topology[member, device] := *epr_edge{from_cid: member, to_cid: $household, rel_type: 'MEMBER_OF'}, *epr_edge{from_cid: member, to_cid: device, rel_type: 'OPERATES_DEVICE'}

rules.name: reciprocity_flow_to
rules.description: Inbound reciprocity flows toward a contributor

rules.name: value_flow_chain
rules.datalog:
value_flow_chain[to, depth] := *epr_edge{from_cid: $start, to_cid: to, rel_type: 'VALUE_FLOW'}, depth = 1
value_flow_chain[to, depth] := value_flow_chain[via, prev], *epr_edge{from_cid: via, to_cid: to, rel_type: 'VALUE_FLOW'}, depth = prev + 1, depth <= $max_depth
